rationale: Rendering and palette pass over the original painterly-cluster block-in — the silhouette, pose, proportions and every design decision are pixel-for-pixel unchanged (all 1496 opaque pixels and 1576 transparent pixels sit exactly where they were); what changed is that each material now carries a full value ramp instead of two or three flat fields. 24 colours became 56. Every material got subdivided and hue-shifted along its ramp, cool in shadow and warm in light: skin runs 8 steps from a plum-cool #3d2129 in the neck's cast shadow up to a warm #ffdcb2 on the forehead and nose tip; olive fatigues run 10 steps from a blue-green #171c21 in the armpit and under the belt to a warm khaki #cbc392 on the shoulder caps; leather runs 9 from near-ink #140c12 to #b3804e on the knuckle plane; hair 7, metal 7, bone 6, rust 6, plus a 5-step cool glass ramp and a 4-step teal emission ramp. The shadow end of every ramp bends toward the plum-black anchor and the light end bends toward warm ochre, so a single form turning from light to dark also turns from warm to cool rather than just getting darker. Form now turns on four stacked passes rather than one: a single upper-left key gradient; a torso cylinder term that puts the lit column left of centre and rolls both edges off; a top-plane term that gives the first row of any new surface a dedicated brighter step, which is what puts the light on the shoulder caps, the forearm tops, the fist knuckles and the boot cuffs; and rim/terminator terms that brighten any pixel whose upper or left neighbour is contour or air and darken the ones facing down-right. Wear and grime were added as clustered blotches, never dithering — the style's no-dither rule still holds. Cloth grain is stretched vertically so it reads as fabric folds; leather grain is stretched horizontally so it reads as creases; metal gets finer specks. On top of that sit hand-placed events: chipped paint scuffed through to primer on both epaulettes, an edge-lit hard corner on the left shoulder plate, a catch-light on the belt buckle, a finger groove and a lit knuckle plane on the near fist, worn boot toes, and a red-cross emblem that is hot on its upper-left arm and grimed down two steps on its lower-right so it reads as painted-on canvas rather than a clean decal. Material transitions are now marked: wherever one material meets another vertically the lower one takes a contact-shadow step and the upper one takes a catch-light step, so collar-to-chest, cuff-to-fist, hem-to-boot and strap-to-goggle all have a real seam. The collar-and-jaw cast shadow across the upper chest — the block-in's biggest single brushstroke — was re-cut as a tapered three-row wedge instead of a rectangle, so it now describes a curved chest. The contour is still one continuous plum-black #120b10, which remains the deepest ink anchor in the file; only true upper-left corners in the top two-thirds lift to #241521 or #3a2330, which reads as light catching a hard edge without breaking the outline. No magenta, no chartreuse, no pure black or white anywhere. Transparency is real: space maps to alpha 0 in a colourType-6 RGBA PNG, no background is baked in, and no interior pixel matches any plausible colour-key value.
frontFacingCue: Four stacked cues, all in value not just colour. (1) A full-width goggle band at rows 9-11: bone rim #cdc4ad over cool glass #8fada6 with two hot #d8fff0 glints, sitting on a dark leather strap — the highest-contrast horizontal event in the sprite and unmistakably a pair of lenses aimed at the camera. (2) A lit forehead plane breaking through the hairline at rows 7-8 in the brightest skin #f2c194, with hair falling on BOTH cheeks (rows 12-15) so the bright face is framed left and right — you cannot read a framed face as a back of a head. (3) A vertical face structure below the goggles: lit nose column, a 4px dark mouth bar at row 15, and a lit chin at rows 16-19. (4) A hard silhouette step at row 16 where the 20px hair mass drops to a 14px bare jaw, which is the classic read for "head, seen from the front". For head/shoulder separation: chin at row 19, a 3-row bare neck in deep shadow #54302f, then a bone field collar (rows 22-26) that is the lightest band in the whole figure, then shoulders only start ramping at row 25 and don't reach full width until row 27 — leaving visible background sky on both sides of the neck. Nothing rises above the shoulder line; the weapon is at hip height and there is no pack. This pass did not touch any of that: the cue geometry is identical, and the added values only reinforce it — the bone collar was pinned to the top of its ramp so it stays the lightest band in the figure, the jaw's cast shadow onto the neck is now an explicit cooler skin step, and the mouth bar was pushed to the darkest skin value so it survives the extra mid-tones around it.
smallCheck: Re-checked with a box-filtered 21x28 downscale inspected at 8x, and it survives better than the flat version did. What holds: the three-band head read (dark hair mass, pale goggle band, lit face) is now stronger, because the forehead and nose sit a step brighter than before and the cheek falls a step cooler, so the bands separate at low resolution instead of averaging together. The bone collar still resolves as a bright pixel row and still lifts the head clear of the shoulders. The rust epaulettes still frame the head as two warm blobs and actually gained saturation. The chest emblem survives as a bright square, the teal injector window survives as one cyan dot, and the two-legged stance plus the lit boot cuffs still hold. The added grime does not turn to noise — because the wear is clustered at 2-3px and oriented along the form, it averages into a slightly mottled mid-tone rather than into static. What is still lost, unchanged from the original verdict: the cross becomes a bright rectangle rather than a cross, and the mouth, nose, thumb and pistol detail all go. The recommendation is unchanged — the emblem wants a dedicated small-size cut rather than a downscale.
